level.title: Supervised vs Unsupervised
level.description: How do we actually teach these machines? Meet the two main methods of learning.

lessons.title: Supervised Learning: The Teacher
lessons.content_md:
# Supervised Learning: The Teacher 👩‍🏫

There are two main ways to teach an AI. The first, and most common, is called **Supervised Learning**.

Imagine a student doing math homework, and a teacher sitting right next to them holding an answer key.
- The student looks at a math problem (the Data).
- The student guesses an answer.
- The teacher immediately says: *"Wrong, the answer is 4."*
- The student adjusts their thinking and tries the next problem.

In Supervised Learning, humans provide the AI with data that is already **labeled** with the correct answers.

For example, we feed the AI 100,000 photos, and every single photo is explicitly tagged by a human as either "Dog" or "Cat". The AI practices guessing, checks the tag to see if it was right, and slowly improves its accuracy.

<flipcard front="👩‍🏫 What is Supervised Learning?" back="Training an AI using data that is already labeled with the correct answers, so the AI can check its work and learn from its mistakes."></flipcard>

lessons.title: Unsupervised Learning: The Messy Room
lessons.content_md:
# Unsupervised Learning: The Messy Room 🧹

The second way to teach an AI is called **Unsupervised Learning**.

Imagine you walk into a giant, messy room filled with thousands of random toys. There is no teacher. There are no labels. There is no answer key.

You tell the AI: *"I don't know what these are. Just organize them into groups that make sense."*

The AI looks at all the toys and starts finding its own patterns. 
- It puts all the round bouncy things in one pile (Balls).
- It puts all the things with wheels in another pile (Cars).
- It puts all the soft fuzzy things in a third pile (Stuffed Animals).

In Unsupervised Learning, we give the AI a massive pile of raw, unlabeled data and ask it to find hidden structures, clusters, or anomalies that humans can't see.

<flipcard front="🧹 What is Unsupervised Learning?" back="Giving an AI raw, unlabeled data and asking it to find hidden patterns or group similar things together on its own, without an answer key."></flipcard>
